title: SSRF: the server fetches what the attacker chose
summary: A link preview, a webhook or an image import makes requests from inside your network. See it reach the cloud metadata service, then defend with an allow-list, no redirects, and an address check at connect time against DNS rebinding.

steps.title: From the outside, through the server, to the inside
body: ```text
attacker ---GET /api/preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/web-role--> shop
shop     ---GET /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/web-role--> 169.254.169.254  (only the shop can reach it)
shop     <--{"AccessKeyId":"...","SecretAccessKey":"...","Token":"..."}--
attacker <--the same JSON, as the 'preview'--

**Server-side request forgery** turns your server into the attacker's proxy. It reaches what they cannot: the cloud **metadata service** at `169.254.169.254` (AWS, Azure, GCP all use that address) with the server's credentials, admin panels on `localhost`, databases and caches on the private network, other tenants' services.

Features that fetch URLs: link previews, webhooks, "import from URL", PDF and image rendering, OAuth/OpenID metadata discovery, XML with external entities (next lesson). The 2019 Capital One breach began with SSRF to the metadata service. SSRF is part of **A01:2025** and **API7:2023**.

steps.prompt: Which mitigation on AWS stops the plain `GET http://169.254.169.254/...` SSRF to steal role credentials, even if the app has the bug?
options: Requiring IMDSv2: a token must first be fetched with a PUT and a special header, which a GET-only SSRF cannot do, and the hop limit of 1 keeps it inside the instance
Using HTTPS for the metadata service
Giving the role fewer permissions only
steps.explain: IMDSv2 is the platform's defence and should be enforced on every instance. Least-privilege roles limit what stolen credentials can do. Neither replaces fixing the SSRF: the internal network is still reachable.

steps.title: Why block-lists lose
body: A block-list for "internal addresses" has to catch every spelling of them:
```text
http://169.254.169.254/           http://2852039166/          (the same IPv4 as one decimal number)
http://0xa9fea9fe/                http://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/   (IPv4-mapped IPv6)
http://cdn.shop.example@169.254.169.254/   (the part before @ is a user name)
http://metadata.attacker.example/   (a DNS name that resolves to 169.254.169.254)
http://cdn.shop.example/redirect?to=http://169.254.169.254/   (an allowed host that redirects)
Defend in this order:
1. **Allow-list** destinations by parsed host (`new Uri(url).IdnHost`), scheme (`https`) and port. Compare the parsed host, never the string.
2. **No automatic redirects** (`SocketsHttpHandler.AllowAutoRedirect = false`), or re-check every hop.

3. **Check the IP you actually connect to**, after DNS: `SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback` resolves the name, refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses, then connects to that same address. That defeats **DNS rebinding** (a name that resolves to a public IP when you check and to `169.254.169.254` a second later, when you fetch).
4. **Network**: send fetches through an egress proxy, and block the metadata address from app containers that do not need it.
5. **Return less**: a preview needs a title, not the body.

steps.prompt: The preview allows only `https://cdn.shop.example` on port 443, parsed with `Uri`. Allowed or refused?
steps.explain: `Uri` lower-cases the host and puts `cdn.shop.example` of the third URL into `UserInfo`; its host is `169.254.169.254`. A string `StartsWith("https://cdn.shop.example")` would have allowed it.

steps.title: An allow-list on the parsed URL
prompt: Write `bool IsAllowedPreviewUrl(string url)`. It is `true` only when `url` is an absolute URI with scheme `https`, the **default port**, **no user info**, and a host (`IdnHost`) that is exactly `cdn.shop.example` or `images.shop.example`, ignoring case. Everything else is `false`, including text that is not a URI.
solution: return Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var u)
hints: `Uri.TryCreate(url, UriKind.Absolute, out var u)` first; then check `u.Scheme`, `u.IsDefaultPort`, `u.UserInfo` and `u.IdnHost`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a spec sheet on the cdn", true, IsAllowedPreviewUrl("https://cdn.shop.example/specs/desk-lamp.html"));

steps.title: The address check, at connect time
body: For webhooks (customers enter any URL, so no host allow-list is possible) the check moves to the moment of connecting:
```csharp fragment
var handler = new SocketsHttpHandler
AllowAutoRedirect = false,
ConnectCallback = async (ctx, ct) =>
var addresses = await Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync(ctx.DnsEndPoint.Host, ct);
var ip = addresses.FirstOrDefault(IsPublicAddress)
?? throw new HttpRequestException("Destination not allowed.");
var socket = new Socket(SocketType.Stream, ProtocolType.Tcp) { NoDelay = true };
await socket.ConnectAsync(ip, ctx.DnsEndPoint.Port, ct);   // the address we checked
return new NetworkStream(socket, ownsSocket: true);
Because the same resolved address is checked and used, a rebinding DNS server gets no second chance. `IsPublicAddress` is the piece to get right: next.

steps.title: IsPublicAddress
prompt: Write `bool IsPublicAddress(IPAddress ip)` (`using System.Net;`). Return `false` for:
- an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) is judged as its IPv4 address.
hints: Map first: `if (ip.IsIPv4MappedToIPv6) ip = ip.MapToIPv4();`. Then `ip.GetAddressBytes()` gives 4 bytes for IPv4, 16 for IPv6.
`172.16.0.0/12` is first byte 172 and second byte 16 to 31. `100.64.0.0/10` is 100 and 64 to 127.
template: Dojo.Eq($"{a} is not public", false, IsPublicAddress(IPAddress.Parse(a)));

steps.title: Live lab: the metadata service, then the allow-list
prompt: In the **vulnerable shop** lab, do **Attack: reach the cloud metadata service** (walk `169.254.169.254` through the shop's link preview) and **Fix: an allow-list, and no redirects** in `Preview.cs`. The check includes the cdn's own open redirect: the allow-list alone is not enough.
steps.explain: An allowed host that redirects is a classic bypass. With `AllowAutoRedirect = false`, the 302 is the end of the request.
